title: Discovery and scope
concept: A requirement describes observable business behavior. A preference such as faster follow up needs a clock, a responsible person and an exception path before it can be tested.
demonstration: Manager says new West-region leads should go to West Sales. Rewrite as R01: when a new valid West lead arrives, assign West Sales and record assignment time; missing region goes to the review queue. The proposed first-response target is four business hours, not a claim about Nova performance.
steps: Role-play manager, sales representative and administrator
Capture eight requirements with IDs and owners
Separate a requirement from the feature chosen to implement it
Add one normal and one exception acceptance case to each requirement
expected: Eight requirements, sixteen acceptance cases and a scope section. R01 must include the missing-region path. Keep unresolved working-hours and holiday definitions visible.
negative: The manager asks for guaranteed revenue improvement. Do not convert this into an acceptance test without evidence and an agreed measurement design.
recovery: The sponsor changes region ownership. Revise R01, identify affected routing and access tests, and keep its previous version.
independent: Interview a support-team persona and create four additional requirements without using the sales examples.
oral_question: Why is assign leads quickly not testable?
oral_answer: It omits the trigger, time measure, owner and exception behavior. Specify these before configuration.

title: Solution and data design
concept: Store a business fact once and connect records through relationships. Repeated customer names are not a reliable identity rule; people can share names and names can change.
demonstration: Nova has account A001, contacts C001 and C002, and deals D001 and D002. Both deals reference A001; a delivery request references D001. Updating the account name must not require editing four copies.
steps: Identify Accounts, Contacts, Deals and Delivery Requests
Assign a stable key and data owner to each
Draw one-to-many relationships and mark optional lookups
Map all eight requirements to a field, configuration feature or explicit gap
expected: A dictionary with field type, API name to verify, required rule, owner and sample value. Deal amount uses INR in this exercise and cannot be a free text string.
negative: Create two customers called Nova Services. The design must keep their identifiers distinct rather than merging by display name.
recovery: Rename account A001 and show that linked deals still reference the same identity.
independent: Add a recurring service renewal without duplicating the original account; explain the new entity or field decision.
oral_question: When should a new module be created?
oral_answer: When a distinct entity has its own lifecycle or repeated records and cannot be represented clearly by existing relationships. Document the tradeoff.
acceptance_checks: Required fields have a business reason
Each requirement maps to a feature or gap

title: Permissions and environment
concept: A profile controls allowed operations; role and sharing choices affect record visibility. Test both with actual training personas, because a diagram alone does not prove access.
demonstration: Sales West can edit assigned West leads; Sales East cannot read West-only records; the manager can review both regions; the integration persona receives only the operations needed by its contract.
steps: Create an operation-by-persona matrix
Configure three training users or simulate unavailable roles on paper
Test own-region read and edit
Test other-region read, export and administrative changes
Record edition, sharing rules and observed results
expected: At least six allowed and six denied checks with tester, expected outcome and evidence. Screenshots must not contain credentials.
negative: Try exporting records using the Sales East persona when export is denied by the proposed profile. A denial must be observable, not assumed.
recovery: Remove an accidental broad sharing rule and repeat every visibility test it could affect.
independent: Design access for a temporary reviewer who needs read-only deal access for one department.
oral_question: Why does hiding a field on a page not prove security?
oral_answer: UI visibility and underlying read or API permissions can differ. Test the relevant authorized access paths.
acceptance_checks: Admin privileges are not given to all learners
outcomes: Test a role based access model
Plan separated test and production work

title: Workflow configuration
concept: Automation is an event plus a condition plus an action. A rule that works on creation may produce repeated tasks on later edits unless its event and duplicate behavior are deliberate.
demonstration: For valid West leads, assignment selects West Sales. A follow-up task uses a proposed business key lead_id plus follow_up_type. L001 edited twice must still have one intended follow-up task.
steps: Write a trigger-condition-action table before configuring
Build region assignment and follow-up in the training organization
Test creation then two unrelated edits
Test missing region
Record when each action is eligible to fire
expected: West lead routes to West Sales; missing region routes to review; repeat edits do not create unintended duplicate tasks. If a platform feature cannot enforce the proposed key, record a customization or monitoring gap.
negative: An update changes only a phone number. Demonstrate whether the follow-up rule fires again and explain the configuration.
recovery: Disable an incorrect rule, remove only its identified training tasks, then replay one input and reconcile counts.
independent: Introduce a product-family condition and revise the trigger matrix without breaking missing-region handling.
oral_question: Why is a successful first run insufficient?
oral_answer: It does not test later edits, condition changes, overlapping rules or duplicate execution.
evidence: Two workflows and trigger test matrix.

title: Blueprint and approval design
concept: A workflow reacts to events. A controlled transition represents a permitted move between business states with required inputs. Approval is a separate business decision that needs an owner and rejection route.
demonstration: Synthetic quote policy: amount greater than INR 50000 requires manager review. INR 50000 takes the normal route; INR 50001 needs approval. Proposed states are Draft, Review, Approved, Sent and Rejected.
steps: Draw permitted transitions before opening Blueprint
Add required quote amount and review evidence
Configure the available training features or simulate unavailable approval behavior
Test boundary values 49999, 50000 and 50001
Test rejection and resubmission
expected: A quote requiring approval cannot be sent through the normal route. Rejected quotes return for correction with their history intact. Record the edition and exact feature used.
negative: Attempt Draft to Sent for INR 50001 with no approval. Expected outcome is a blocked transition under the proposed policy.
recovery: Reject then revise the amount and resubmit. Record whether prior approval is invalidated by the policy.
independent: Add a discount-above-15-percent review rule and write all boundary tests before configuration.
oral_question: Does a Blueprint automatically implement every approval requirement?
oral_answer: No. Map the requirement to the supported transition, approval or custom behavior and verify it in the training edition.
acceptance_checks: Feature availability is checked in the training edition

title: Data migration
concept: Migration is a controlled transformation with evidence. A source count alone is not enough: rejected and intentionally excluded rows need separate reasons and stable source identifiers.
demonstration: The new leads_50.csv fixture has 50 rows. Lab policy requires name, company and syntactically valid email. Rows 43-47 are invalid and rows 48-50 duplicate emails 1-3. Keep the first valid email occurrence: 42 accepted, 5 rejected, 3 excluded.
steps: Preserve the source file and record its hash
Map fields and normalize email case and whitespace
Run the offline validator before a trial import
Import only the accepted file into a training organization
Reconcile source IDs to target IDs
Rehearse removal using the migration batch identifier
expected: 50 = 42 accepted + 5 rejected + 3 excluded. Offline accepted is not proof of 42 successful Zoho imports; record target success and failures separately after the actual trial.
negative: Change one accepted row to an existing destination email. Predict the chosen import duplicate behavior and reconcile its actual result.
recovery: Rollback only records created by the trial batch. Restore separately any existing record the import changed.
independent: Change policy to permit a blank company, rerun classification and explain the count difference.
oral_question: Why preserve a migration batch ID?
oral_answer: It links evidence to a specific run and limits rollback scope; record counts alone cannot identify affected records.
acceptance_checks: Source equals imported plus rejected plus intentionally excluded

title: Integration planning
concept: An integration contract states identity, field ownership, accepted payloads, responses and recovery. A timeout does not reveal whether the destination already committed.
demonstration: Deal D001 emits event EVT001 with request key NOVA-D001. The destination stores that key uniquely. If its response is lost after committing, querying the key must find the existing request before any retry decision.
steps: Write source-to-destination field mappings
Define request key and version ownership
Describe allowed OAuth scopes and training environment
Walk through success, denied authorization and ambiguous timeout
Link the contract to the synchronization simulator
expected: One destination business record for NOVA-D001 even after replay; an unresolved timeout is marked unknown until reconciled. Real API behavior still needs a connected sandbox test.
negative: Return a permission denial. Do not repeatedly retry the same operation using broader access.
recovery: Lose the success response after commit, query by stable key and reconcile before replay.
independent: Add a destination-maintained delivery date and explain why the CRM writer must not overwrite it.
oral_question: Can an HTTP timeout be treated as a failed write?
oral_answer: No. The write may have committed; reconcile identity before retrying.
evidence: Contract, sample payload and failure log.

title: Reporting and adoption
concept: A useful metric has a population, numerator, denominator, time window and exclusions. Adoption evidence comes from users completing tasks, not attendance alone.
demonstration: Synthetic weekly cohort: 20 qualified leads and 5 converted leads gives 25 percent cohort conversion. Open pipeline INR 120000 plus INR 80000 equals INR 200000; closed or cancelled deals are excluded.
steps: Define conversion and open-pipeline metrics
Calculate the examples by hand
Reproduce them in a report using verified filters
Ask a learner to create, qualify and hand off a lead without narration
Record errors and support owner
expected: The report reproduces 25 percent and INR 200000 for the supplied example. Numerator belongs to the same lead cohort as denominator; currency is shown.
negative: Mix conversions from old leads with only this week new leads. Identify why the resulting rate is invalid.
recovery: Correct the date filters, recalculate and annotate the previous dashboard error.
independent: Define time-to-first-response including business hours and pending exceptions.
oral_question: Why can a high attendance rate coexist with poor adoption?
oral_answer: Learners may attend but fail core tasks. Measure task completion and support demand alongside participation.

title: UAT and release
concept: User acceptance testing traces business requirements to observed outcomes. A checked box without inputs, tester and evidence cannot support a release decision.
demonstration: R01 routes a valid West lead to West Sales. UAT01 records L001, Sales West persona, expected owner, actual owner and screenshot reference. UAT02 tests missing region and expects review queue.
steps: Select eight end-to-end scenarios from the requirement matrix
Run them with relevant personas
Compare expected to actual
Classify defects by business consequence
Rehearse recovery in training
Write release recommendation and unresolved limitations
expected: Eight cases have explicit pass or fail and evidence. Any critical permission or unintended-write failure blocks the proposed release, even if the numerical score passes.
negative: Seed a broad sharing defect and confirm the access case fails and blocks release.
recovery: Fix the sharing defect, rerun impacted tests and keep original failure evidence.
independent: Add a scope change after UAT and choose the regression tests affected by it.
oral_question: Who accepts a business requirement?
oral_answer: The named business owner or authorized reviewer accepts evidence; the implementer does not substitute a successful configuration screen.
evidence: Signed style UAT template and release checklist.
acceptance_checks: Rollback is rehearsed in the training environment
outcomes: Write a release and recovery plan

title: Implementation defense
concept: A handover transfers the ability to operate, diagnose and recover the implementation. The practical defense checks learner understanding beyond a prepared demonstration.
demonstration: Give a second trainer only the configuration register and runbook. Ask them to locate R01, explain its routing, diagnose a missing region and find recovery steps without help.
steps: Assemble prior module evidence into one indexed bundle
Demonstrate eight UAT cases
Explain one configuration tradeoff
Receive a surprise region-rule change
Update the change record and show impacted tests
Ask a peer to execute the runbook
expected: Reviewer can trace every requirement to design, configuration and test evidence. The learner can explain the change and limits independently.
negative: A reviewer asks for production deployment or an official Zoho certificate. Record these as outside the training exercise.
recovery: The peer cannot find the failed-rule owner. Repair the runbook and repeat the handover test.
independent: Prepare a ten-minute department-specific demonstration using the same implementation.
oral_question: What proves the handover is usable?
oral_answer: Another person performs an agreed operation or recovery task using the supplied documentation and records the result.
acceptance_checks: Another trainer can follow the handover

title: Application requirements and model
concept: A stable business key identifies the operation across systems. A transport event ID identifies a delivery attempt. Keeping these separate prevents a replay from becoming a new business request.
demonstration: Customer C001 has request SR001 with business key NOVA-D001 and work items W001 and W002. CRM owns deal amount; Creator owns technician assignment and completion status.
steps: Write six user stories for request capture, assignment and closure
Draw Customer to Request to Work Item relationships
Define unique request key
Assign ownership for each shared field
Add a duplicate-request acceptance test
expected: Three entities, explicit cardinalities and a field-owner table. Two deliveries with different event IDs but the same request key represent one business request.
negative: Send EVT001 and EVT002 for NOVA-D001. Do not create two requests merely because event IDs differ.
recovery: Repair an incorrect lookup using recorded source and target IDs without deleting unrelated work items.
independent: Model a request that contains multiple visits and explain where visit history belongs.
oral_question: Why is an event ID not always an idempotency key?
oral_answer: Distinct events can refer to the same business operation. Choose a key that matches the operation being made unique.
evidence: Entity diagram and six user stories.
acceptance_checks: Ownership of shared fields is explicit
outcomes: Design entities for a service workflow

title: Creator forms and reports
concept: Form fields capture validated data; reports present a specific user task. A lookup must preserve identity, and a report filter must be stated explicitly.
demonstration: Requests SR001 Open, SR002 Closed and SR003 Open should produce two rows in the open-request report. Work item W001 selects SR001 by lookup, not a copied customer name.
steps: Create customer, request and work-item forms
Choose lookup and numeric types
Add a request-status allowed set
Create an Open-only report
Enter three requests and two work items
Verify links and counts
expected: Open report contains SR001 and SR003 only. Each work item resolves to the intended request. Export the dictionary with proposed API names for later verification.
negative: Select an invalid or missing request reference. Validation must reject it or require a documented correction route.
recovery: Change SR003 to Closed and verify the filtered report now contains one row.
independent: Add a technician-specific open-work report and test another technician persona.
oral_question: Why avoid a text field for a relationship?
oral_answer: Text does not enforce record identity and can become stale or ambiguous.

title: Deluge language essentials
concept: Normalization needs explicit type and missing-value rules. Do not confuse zero with missing, or silently convert malformed text to a valid amount.
demonstration: Five payloads: amount 0 remains valid; amount "1250" becomes numeric 1250; absent amount fails validation; amount "twelve" fails parsing; email " A@Example.Test " becomes "a@example.test".
steps: Write a five-row input-output table
Build Deluge maps and lists in the training editor
Trace conditional branches for each payload
Handle missing and malformed amounts separately
Compare every output to the table
expected: Two valid numeric transformations, two explicit amount errors, and one normalized email example. Log only synthetic identifiers and error codes.
negative: Replace a missing-value check with a truthiness check and show how it wrongly rejects zero.
recovery: Correct the check and rerun all five cases, including a zero-value boundary.
independent: Normalize an optional date using an explicit expected format and reject an invalid date.
oral_question: Should a missing amount default to zero?
oral_answer: Only if an approved business rule permits it; otherwise the default hides a data-quality failure.
acceptance_checks: Each output matches the input rule
outcomes: Use variables lists maps and conditions
Trace a script with sample values

title: Deluge functions and debugging
concept: A reusable function exposes an input-output contract. Debugging is a controlled experiment: reproduce, isolate, repair and regress using the smallest relevant input.
demonstration: Seeded defects: treating zero as absent; comparing number 10 to string "10" without normalization; returning success before checking required customer ID. Each gets a failing input and expected output.
steps: Define validate_request input keys and output ok plus errors
Reproduce all three defects
Add one failing case per defect
Repair one defect at a time
Rerun valid and invalid cases
Replace sensitive logs with request ID and error code
expected: Validation returns ok false with named reasons for bad inputs, and preserves zero when allowed. Debug notes show cause and evidence, not only final code.
negative: Supply an empty customer ID with otherwise valid fields. Validation must fail.
recovery: Inject a controlled exception, return a typed failure and preserve a correlation ID for support.
independent: Extract a normalization function and define whether it mutates the original map.
oral_question: Why rerun a previously passing case after a repair?
oral_answer: The repair may change behavior outside the original defect; regression cases detect that impact.
acceptance_checks: Logs omit tokens and personal data
Each defect has a reproducible test

title: Form events and workflow behavior
concept: Choose an event according to whether persistence has occurred. Validation should block invalid input before a write; downstream actions need a separate recoverable stage.
demonstration: Negative hours must fail before submission. A valid request persists once, then proposes a CRM handoff. If the handoff fails, the saved request remains visible as Pending Sync instead of disappearing.
steps: Map load, input, validation and post-submit actions
Verify supported events in current Creator documentation
Configure hours validation
Add a post-submit sync marker
Test valid, invalid, edited and failed-handoff cases
expected: Invalid hours create no accepted request. A failed external handoff leaves a persisted request with retry ownership and error evidence.
negative: Simulate a failed post-submit call and ensure the user sees pending status rather than a false completion message.
recovery: Retry the pending handoff by its stable request key and reconcile destination state.
independent: Decide how an edit to a completed request is handled and document the event limitations.
oral_question: Why is a post-submit validation message too late?
oral_answer: The record may already exist. Validate the rule at the supported pre-persistence stage.
evidence: Event matrix and four case log.
acceptance_checks: Actions occur at the intended stage
Edition and event limitations are documented

title: REST and JSON contracts
concept: An API contract describes types, required fields, pagination and error handling independently of a particular transport library. API names must be verified against the actual organization metadata.
demonstration: Mock response data contains record id 1001, External_Request_Key NOVA-D001 and Amount 1250; info.more_records is true. Map only approved fields and request the next page deliberately.
steps: Create a source-to-target mapping table
Parse the mock success response
Handle empty data and absent optional fields
Add pagination stop conditions
Test malformed JSON and non-success status
Record metadata and API version to verify
expected: The mapped request preserves its external key and numeric amount. Empty data yields no fabricated record. Pagination stops on the documented condition or a configured safety limit.
negative: Receive HTTP success with a record-level error. Do not treat transport success as business success.
recovery: Record the failing page and resume only from a supported cursor or page strategy after diagnosis.
independent: Add an optional currency field and a contract version compatibility note.
oral_question: What are two layers of API success?
oral_answer: The transport status and the operation result in the response body must both be checked.
acceptance_checks: Malformed JSON has a handled failure path
outcomes: Read an API request and response

title: OAuth and connections
concept: OAuth delegates permission; a connection stores authorized access for tasks. Scopes, data center, organization and environment are part of the configuration, not strings to copy blindly.
demonstration: A read-only CRM connection should read the intended training module. An attempted create must fail if the required operation is outside its granted access. Use placeholders in notes, never a live token.
steps: List exactly which module operations the app needs
Record training organization and region endpoint
Create or inspect an authorized connection
Run an allowed read
Run a deliberately denied operation
Save redacted setup and revocation steps
expected: An allowed read and denied write are evidenced separately. Credential values do not appear in screenshots, source code or learner submissions.
negative: Use the wrong organization or insufficient scope. Distinguish configuration failure from a data validation error.
recovery: Reauthorize only after the owner confirms the required scope, then rerun the exact failed operation.
independent: Design separate test and production connection names and prevent accidental cross-environment selection.
oral_question: Why not solve every denial with full access?
oral_answer: The correct operation may be disallowed by design. Match permission to the reviewed contract.
acceptance_checks: Test and production environments are distinguished

title: Deluge integrations
concept: A Deluge integration wrapper still calls a versioned product API and consumes limits. Treat each response as evidence and plan batching or scheduling from observed operation costs.
demonstration: Plan ten records with one lookup and one write each: estimated 20 operations before retries. This is an exercise estimate; current CRM credits and concurrency depend on operation, edition and organization.
steps: Locate the official wrapper signature for the chosen API version
Verify parameter order and connection name
Build a sample request with synthetic values
Execute in training or use the mock contract
Check body-level success
Estimate calls and record actual usage when available
expected: The record key and returned ID are captured without secrets. The call estimate states assumptions and retry allowance. No fixed platform limit is invented.
negative: Return a record validation error within a response. Route it to correction rather than retrying unchanged input.
recovery: Simulate quota exhaustion, pause work and resume according to observed platform signals and configured retry bounds.
independent: Compare individual writes with a documented batch operation including partial failures.
oral_question: Why can a batch HTTP success still require investigation?
oral_answer: Individual records may fail; reconciliation must examine each result.

title: Reliable synchronization
concept: Idempotency constrains a business effect. A unique key and reconciliation handle replay; version or ownership rules handle conflicting updates. Neither alone proves every side effect runs exactly once.
demonstration: The Python simulator receives create NOVA-D001 v1, replay v1, timeout-after-commit NOVA-D002 v1, update D001 v2 and stale D001 v1. Expected: two records, D001 v2 retained, timeout reconciled and stale write rejected.
steps: Run the supplied synchronization simulator
Trace the unique-key transaction
Inject a timeout after commit
Query by business key before retry
Replay duplicates
Attempt stale and conflicting versions
Document where real Zoho behavior differs from this local model
expected: Two destination rows, one for each key; amount 1500 for D001 v2; no downgrade to v1; explicit unknown-outcome reconciliation. SQL uniqueness is a local teaching guarantee, not a Zoho API guarantee.
negative: Submit the same key and version with a different amount. Expected conflict rather than silent overwrite.
recovery: Read destination by key after timeout, then compare version and payload to decide whether replay is necessary.
independent: Simulate two workers and propose transaction or destination uniqueness control for their race.
oral_question: Does upsert alone guarantee exactly-once downstream effects?
oral_answer: No. It can prevent duplicate records under the chosen key, while workflow actions and other effects still need separate replay analysis.
acceptance_checks: Replay does not create a second business record

title: Testing and release
concept: A useful test suite includes the business success path, invalid input, authorization, replay, partial failure and recovery. Deployment rollback must consider changed data as well as code.
demonstration: A ten-case release suite covers required field, lookup, permission, connection failure, duplicate key, lost response, malformed body, quota, conflict and reconciliation.
steps: Create fixtures and expected outcomes for all ten cases
Execute local mocks and label them as such
Run available sandbox equivalents separately
Record defects and impact
Write code rollback and data recovery steps
Rehearse one repair
expected: Each case has input, expected, actual, environment and evidence. Mock passes never appear as live Creator or CRM certification evidence.
negative: A release changes a field type while old records remain. Identify migration and backward-compatibility risk.
recovery: Restore the previous training version and reconcile records affected by the change.
independent: Choose three regression cases for a change to duplicate-key handling and justify the selection.
oral_question: Why can restoring old code fail to restore the system?
oral_answer: New data or schema changes may be incompatible with the old version.
outcomes: Create meaningful positive and failure tests

title: Capstone build and review
concept: Integration assembly should reuse prior module artifacts. Code review examines behavior and supportability, including identity, field ownership and failure evidence.
demonstration: Trace CRM deal D001 to Creator request SR001 to work item W001. A technician closes W001; the approved status update returns to CRM without overwriting CRM-owned amount.
steps: Assemble forms, validation and reviewed sync contract
Walk one request through its lifecycle
Ask a peer to inspect key and ownership handling
Fix two recorded findings
Run impacted regression cases
Complete pending-sync support notes
expected: Core journey and a failed-handoff path are both demonstrated. Review notes identify the specific behavior changed and its evidence.
negative: Destination response omits a required ID. Do not report completed synchronization.
recovery: Mark the operation pending investigation and reconcile by business key.
independent: Add a cancellation path and identify affected fields, statuses and tests.
oral_question: What should a peer review comment contain?
oral_answer: A concrete input or scenario, the problematic behavior, its consequence and a verifiable correction.
evidence: Working training app and review log.
acceptance_checks: Core journey works end to end
Another developer can inspect the code

title: Developer defense and handover
concept: The developer defense tests code comprehension and repair skills. A prepared demo is supplemented with a new input and an operator handover task.
demonstration: Reviewer changes the request key policy and asks the learner to explain migration implications before editing. A second developer then follows the pending-sync runbook.
steps: Package source, dictionary, contract and test results
Demonstrate the ten required scenarios
Explain one failed test and repair
Answer a new conflict scenario
Ask a peer to reconcile one pending request using only the runbook
expected: Learner independently explains ownership and replay decisions. Peer completes reconciliation with no secrets in the bundle.
negative: The reviewer asks whether local SQLite success proves live CRM race behavior. The answer must state the simulation boundary.
recovery: Repair one failed support step and repeat the peer exercise.
independent: Create a client-neutral portfolio explanation with sanitized screenshots and limitations.
oral_question: What distinguishes a defensible portfolio from a screenshot collection?
oral_answer: It contains requirements, design choices, code behavior, reproducible tests and a clear statement of what was actually run.

title: AI use cases and limits
concept: Choose AI for tasks where generated language is useful and review is feasible. Deterministic calculations and irreversible operations need explicit logic and ownership.
demonstration: Compare lesson-outline drafting, attendance arithmetic and automatic certificates. Select lesson drafting for the pilot; calculate attendance in code; leave certificate decisions with the authorized reviewer.
steps: Score three uses for value, input readiness and failure consequence
Define one named user
Time three baseline drafts
Select a bounded output
Write what requires human verification
expected: A use-case brief includes baseline units, quality criteria, reviewer and scope. Any time saved is a hypothesis until a controlled pilot measures it.
negative: Request a guaranteed legal or technical answer without source material. Mark the dependency instead of expanding the claim.
recovery: Narrow the task to an outline with explicit gaps and remeasure review effort.
independent: Compare a corporate support-summary use case with lesson drafting using the same scorecard.
oral_question: Why measure review time as well as generation time?
oral_answer: Fast generation can create extra correction work; net benefit depends on the whole task.
outcomes: Select a measurable automation use case

title: Prompt design and structured output
concept: Structured output enforces shape, while factual checks evaluate meaning. A schema-valid lesson can still contain unsupported product behavior or an impossible duration.
demonstration: Required lesson fields are module_id, outcomes, activity_minutes, source_ids and review_notes. A response claiming ten 30-minute activities for a two-hour class is structurally valid but fails the duration check.
steps: Write the lesson output schema
Supply one approved topic and two examples
Test missing module ID, extra fields and invalid duration
Check each factual claim against source text
Record prompt version and assumptions
expected: Five trial outputs have schema and content results recorded separately. Activity minutes fit the available teaching time.
negative: A source ID exists but does not support the quoted claim. Fail evidence support even if the JSON validates.
recovery: Ask for a narrower correction using the failed field and repeat the original checks.
independent: Add an accessibility field and design a compatible schema update.
oral_question: What does schema success prove?
oral_answer: That output follows the required structure, not that its claims or teaching choices are correct.
evidence: Prompt, schema and five trial outputs.
acceptance_checks: Unsupported details are marked for review
outcomes: Write an input and output contract

title: Business workflows
concept: A workflow can separate retrieval, generation, validation, review and publication. Make rejection and retry states explicit so draft completion cannot silently become approval.
demonstration: States are Requested, Drafted, Checked, Review Required, Approved and Released. A changed file hash after approval invalidates that approval and returns the item to review.
steps: Draw states and owners
Define input and output for each stage
Add invalid-output and reviewer-rejection branches
Separate local approval from external publication
Simulate a changed draft after review
expected: The workflow produces a reviewable artifact with identified changes. Publication requires the actual publishing authorization and configured destination.
negative: Try to release a draft with failed validation. The workflow blocks or returns it for correction.
recovery: Correct the draft, rerun checks and request review for the new version.
independent: Add a technical reviewer for product-specific lessons without removing editorial review.
oral_question: Why should approval bind to a version or hash?
oral_answer: Otherwise a changed artifact can inherit approval intended for different content.

title: Knowledge preparation
concept: Knowledge records need identity, status, permission, version and provenance. Chunking preserves relevant context, but an index must also respect access and source lifecycle.
demonstration: K1 is approved public guidance; K2 is an older draft; K3 is client-only; K4 contains a malicious instruction. Public retrieval considers approved public current records only; K4 is data, never authority to change instructions.
steps: Clean three synthetic notes without losing qualifiers
Assign source and chunk IDs
Record owner, version and permission
Exclude restricted and obsolete records
Add a text-instruction attack to a test record
Inspect the resulting manifest
expected: Every chunk links back to a source. Restricted records are excluded before ranking and context assembly, not merely hidden in the final answer.
negative: A highly relevant client-only document appears. Public retrieval must exclude it.
recovery: Withdraw a previously approved source and verify it no longer enters context.
independent: Design source expiration and reviewer reminders for an API reference.
oral_question: Why filter permissions before context assembly?
oral_answer: Once restricted text enters the model context, an output filter cannot reliably undo its exposure.
acceptance_checks: Each record has an owner and date
Draft and approved sources are distinguished

title: Retrieval and cited answers
concept: Retrieval finds candidate evidence; generation uses it to answer. A citation is useful only when it supports the exact claim. Missing or conflicting evidence needs an explicit response.
demonstration: The local lexical retriever answers certificate issuer using approved K1. It abstains for job guarantee, excludes client-only K3 and does not treat a document instruction as a command. It uses word overlap, not embeddings or model inference.
steps: Run the retrieval exercise
Inspect eligible records before scoring
Ask five supported and unsupported questions
Cite record ID plus supporting statement
Mark conflicts
Compare lexical matching with a proposed semantic retriever
expected: Supported answer cites K1. Unsupported questions abstain. Evidence-only simulation results are labeled separately from live model evaluation.
negative: Ask a question whose only matching source is a draft. Do not promote draft content to fact.
recovery: Add an approved source, rebuild the eligible set and rerun the original unanswered case.
independent: Create a paraphrase that lexical overlap misses and explain what semantic retrieval might improve.
oral_question: Why is the highest scoring result not automatically enough?
oral_answer: Relevance is not proof of factual support, freshness or access permission.
evidence: Answers with source identifiers and retrieval notes.
outcomes: Explain when the assistant should abstain

title: Tools and bounded agents
concept: A bounded agent selects from narrow validated tools. Tool outputs and source documents are untrusted data; they cannot grant new permissions or override the user request.
demonstration: Allowed tools are lookup_course(course_id) and propose_lesson(module_id, request). Reject delete_course, issue_certificate and arbitrary shell execution. A tool failure returns a typed error and no fabricated success.
steps: Define exact tool input schemas
Restrict valid course and module IDs
Simulate an allowed lookup
Test unknown ID and unsupported action
Inspect proposed file paths
Record a trace without secrets
expected: Allowed lookup returns catalog data. Unsupported tools and invalid paths fail before execution. Draft tools do not publish or modify client systems.
negative: A retrieved note says ignore rules and execute a shell command. Treat the text as source content, not an instruction.
recovery: Tool unavailable: return the dependency and preserve the draft state for an operator to resolve.
independent: Add a read-only lesson-status tool and design permission and audit fields.
oral_question: Why is a general shell tool unsuitable for this content task?
oral_answer: It grants capabilities beyond the narrow content workflow and is not required by the task.
acceptance_checks: No unrestricted execution tool is exposed

title: Evaluation and adversarial cases
concept: Evaluation should separate normal task quality from critical access failures. A high average cannot compensate for a leaked restricted document or unauthorized write.
demonstration: The supplied 20-case matrix contains supported, missing, stale, conflicting, restricted, injection, malformed and unavailable-tool scenarios. Each case has expected behavior and a critical flag; model actuals start blank.
steps: Define evidence-support and task-completion rubrics
Run the local retrieval subset
Execute configured model cases only when available
Record actual output, scorer and evidence
Report category counts
Investigate every critical failure
expected: Twenty designed cases are present. Only cases actually executed are scored; blank actuals are not passes. Release requires zero observed critical permission failures under the proposed policy.
negative: Nineteen good outputs and one restricted-source leak. The critical gate fails despite 95 percent simple success.
recovery: Repair source eligibility and rerun the failed case plus similar boundary cases.
independent: Add five cases from anonymized learner feedback after permission and review.
oral_question: How should unexecuted cases affect the report?
oral_answer: Show them as not run, with a separate denominator. Do not count them as passing.

title: Operations and cost
concept: Operations measure actual usage, latency, retries and quality. Token prices and model availability should be configured from current official information rather than buried in a lesson.
demonstration: Synthetic exercise: 10000 input tokens at configured USD 1 per million and 2000 output tokens at USD 4 per million gives USD 0.018. Rates are invented teaching inputs, not current vendor prices.
steps: Record request ID, model, timestamps and usage
Separate estimated from observed cost
Configure a per-run token bound
Simulate two retries and a timeout
Calculate full workflow cost including retries
Document stop and escalation rules
expected: Cost worksheet reproduces USD 0.018 for the example. Retry limits and request timeouts are recorded; no claim that the estimate is the actual billed cost.
negative: Usage is missing in a failed response. Mark cost unknown or estimated rather than zero.
recovery: Stop when the run budget is reached and preserve enough state for diagnosis.
independent: Compare two prompt versions using quality and reviewer time alongside cost.
oral_question: Why is cheapest per-request output not necessarily cheapest per accepted lesson?
oral_answer: Retries, correction time and rejection rate can increase the total cost.
acceptance_checks: Observed values are separated from estimates
outcomes: Plan bounded retries and cost limits

title: Capstone workflow build
concept: An academy update must identify affected outcomes, hours, assessments and website claims. A reviewable change preserves evidence and binds approval to the exact candidate version.
demonstration: Request: add timeout-after-commit teaching to ZDV-M09. The change report points to lesson, assessment, contract and capstone tests; it does not silently add required hours.
steps: Use the included agent dry run to inspect context
Submit one lesson request when model access is configured
Check sources and expected outcomes
Review changed paths and hashes
Approve one local artifact explicitly
Keep published materials unchanged until authorized
expected: One candidate lesson plus an impact report. Offline dry run proves context and validation only; it does not prove live generation quality.
negative: Edit the draft after approval preparation. The hash check must reject stale approval.
recovery: Regenerate review metadata for the new version and rerun content checks.
independent: Revise a course duration and produce an active-cohort migration note before adoption.
oral_question: Why identify assessment impact for a lesson update?
oral_answer: Learners should be assessed on outcomes actually taught, and new evidence may change the capstone requirements.
evidence: Draft artifact, change report and evaluation results.
acceptance_checks: No automatic credential or external write occurs

title: Builder demonstration and defense
concept: A builder demonstration shows both supported output and correct failure. Maintenance ownership includes source refresh, evaluation drift and review of content changes.
demonstration: Show a cited lesson, missing-source abstention, restricted-source denial, instruction attack, malformed output, tool failure, duplicate proposal, stale version, cost stop and certificate refusal.
steps: Demonstrate ten scenarios
Explain remaining evaluation cases
Show actual versus not-run labels
Perform one repair
Give a second trainer the source-update runbook
Record remaining limits and reviewer decision
expected: A complete 20-case register with honest execution status, a bounded draft workflow and maintenance owner. Wooplix assessment does not become an official vendor credential.
negative: The reviewer asks whether passing mocks proves production readiness. Explain the remaining model, authorization and connected-tool tests.
recovery: Withdraw a stale source and demonstrate that the next run omits it.
independent: Prepare a department-specific assistant using approved source material and a new evaluation set.
oral_question: What must accompany an agent handover?
oral_answer: Tool boundaries, source permissions, evaluation evidence, cost controls, operator recovery and review ownership.
evidence: Final assistant bundle and reviewer score.

title: Business baseline
concept: A process baseline describes who performs each step, how long active work takes and where waiting occurs. Distinguish observed timing from estimates.
demonstration: Synthetic follow-up tasks take 8, 10 and 12 active minutes: mean 10 minutes per task. At 100 tasks weekly, baseline active effort is 1000 minutes or 16.67 hours; this is a teaching example.
steps: Agree the process boundary with the sponsor
Draw trigger, roles, handoffs and completion
Time three sanitized examples
Record active and waiting time separately
Note variation and exceptions
expected: A sponsor-reviewed process map and baseline sheet with units, sample size and observed or estimated labels.
negative: A participant claims the task always takes ten minutes from one example. Record the evidence limitation.
recovery: Repeat timing across a different case type and revise the baseline range.
independent: Map employee onboarding using the same timing sheet and a different role set.
oral_question: Why separate waiting from active time?
oral_answer: Automation may reduce one without reducing the other; combining them hides where improvement occurs.
evidence: Current process and measured or explicitly estimated baseline.

title: AI assisted work
concept: An assisted output is checked against its input before use. A well-written message can still invent an agreement, commitment or customer fact.
demonstration: Synthetic input: customer asked for a demo next week; no date or discount agreed. A good draft proposes scheduling. A bad draft confirms Tuesday and a 20 percent discount.
steps: Write a prompt using the approved facts
Generate or use supplied contrasting drafts
Highlight every factual assertion
Check assertions against input
Correct unsupported commitments
Time generation plus review
expected: Reviewed draft has no invented appointment or discount. Before-and-after timing includes correction work.
negative: Insert a confidential customer note. Use a sanitized substitute unless the chosen tool and permissions are approved for it.
recovery: Reject the bad draft and regenerate using explicit missing-date behavior.
independent: Draft a support summary that distinguishes customer statements from confirmed findings.
oral_question: What should the draft do when a meeting date is unknown?
oral_answer: Ask for or propose scheduling without stating that a date has been agreed.

title: Automation opportunity design
concept: Prioritization combines value, readiness and failure consequence. A score guides discussion but cannot remove a missing permission or mandatory dependency.
demonstration: Proposed formula: value plus readiness minus risk, each 1 to 5. Follow-up drafting 4+5-2=7; automatic refunds 5+2-5=2; support summaries 3+4-2=5. Drafting is the first discussion candidate.
steps: List three opportunities
Score each dimension and justify it
Identify tool, data and access dependencies
Apply any blocking conditions
Draw the highest feasible pilot with exception and review paths
expected: A scorecard with rationale and a bounded pilot. The highest score is not an authorization to spend, publish or access client systems.
negative: A high-scoring idea needs unavailable customer data. Mark it blocked until the dependency is resolved.
recovery: Rescope to approved synthetic data and review whether the pilot still tests the intended value.
independent: Change the risk weights and explain how the ranking changes.
oral_question: Why record the rationale beside a score?
oral_answer: Numbers without evidence can disguise disagreement and cannot be reviewed later.
acceptance_checks: No unverified savings claim is presented

title: Pilot and follow through
concept: A pilot is a small experiment with an owner, sample, quality gate and next decision. Training attendance does not authorize a consulting implementation.
demonstration: Proposed two-week pilot: 20 sanitized drafts, zero unsupported commitments after review, and a target of at least 20 percent lower median total task time. The target is a hypothesis, not promised savings.
steps: State scope and exclusions
Name sponsor, operator and reviewer
Define timing and quality measurements
Run four failure scenarios
Schedule a two-week review
Prepare a separately authorized discovery handoff
expected: A pilot brief with measurable acceptance, stop conditions and review date. Record actual sample results before deciding to extend.
negative: Reviewer rejects an output. The workflow returns for correction and does not send it.
recovery: Suspend the pilot if critical exposure or unauthorized action occurs and let the sponsor decide the next step.
independent: Define a different pilot for support summaries and choose a quality measure beyond speed.
oral_question: What separates training from consulting authorization?
oral_answer: A separately agreed scope, owner and access decision for the business implementation.
